description: The bar chart illustrates the GLUE performance of various fine-tuning methods applied to two sizes of the RoBERTa model — base (blue bars) and large (orange bars) — across seven different tuning strategies: Prefix, Adaptor, LoRA, BitFit, S₁-model, S₄-model, and S₅-model. The vertical axis represents GLUE Performance, ranging from approximately 85 to 89, with tick marks at 86, 87, 88, and 89. The horizontal axis lists the fine-tuning methods, with each method represented by a pair of adjacent bars indicating performance for base and large models respectively. RoBERTa-large consistently outperforms RoBERTa-base across all methods, with the largest performance gap observed in the S₅-model (large ~89.2 vs. base ~87.0). The highest overall performance is achieved by the S₅-model with RoBERTa-large (~89.2), followed closely by LoRA with RoBERTa-large (~89.0). In contrast, BitFit with RoBERTa-base shows the lowest performance (~85.1), while its large counterpart reaches ~87.7. The S₁-model shows nearly identical performance for both model sizes (~85.5), suggesting limited benefit from scaling up the model for this method. The chart also includes two random baselines (S₀-model and S₃-model) mentioned in the caption, though they are not visually represented in the chart — only S₁, S₄, and S₅ are plotted. The legend in the top-left corner clearly distinguishes between “base” and “large” using color-coded squares. Overall, the chart highlights that larger models and certain parameter-efficient tuning methods (especially LoRA and S₅-model) yield superior GLUE scores.
